div.head: Duns 6.2
div.ab: Swa eac ælc ðe gewita oððe gewyrhta sy, ðær utlendisc man inlendiscan derie, geladie ðære midwiste be ðes orfes weorðe; ⁊ þæt sy cyreað; ⁊ se ðe hyne belecge, ofga his spræce mid foraðe.

Sic omnis qui cooperans uel conscius sit, ubi unlandiscus homo inlandiscum derie (id est extraneus indigenam noceat), adlegiet se super conscientia illa secundum precium captalis; et hoc iusiurando electo, quod dicitur cyreað. Et qui eum impetit, inducat causam suam mid foraðe (id est cum preiuratione).

So auch jeder [andere], der [als] Mitwisser oder Beihelfer [verklagt] ist, wo ein ausländischer Mann einen inländischen schädigt, reinige sich von solcher Mitwissenschaft [durch Eid] in Höhe des [verlorenen] Viehwerthes; und dies sei ein Eid mit [vom Gegner] ernannten [Helfern]; und wer ihn beschuldigt, beginne seine Klage durch Klage-Eid.

So also let everyone [else] who [is accused as] accessory or helper, where a foreign man harms a native, clear himself of such complicity [by oath] to the value of the [lost] cattle; and let this be an oath with [helpers] nominated [by the opponent]; and let whoever accuses him begin his suit with a fore-oath.

Let every one that is cognisant or complicit where a stranger injures a native clear himself of such complicity [by an oath] to the value of the [lost] livestock, and [that oath] is to be a select oath [cyre-a‏‏þ]; and he who accuses him shall begin his case with a foreoath.
div.note: U: translator unrecorded: check; K: ‘cooperaus’ corrected to ‘cooperans’ (a misreading); spacing tidied. Liebermann compares II As 1.1 and 23.2.

note.seg: so M Hk; inl. R T; vielleicht hatte Quadr.-Orig. utl.
thus M Hk; inl. R T; perhaps the original of Quadr. had utl.

Der vorige Satz wird verallgemeinert zum Fall der Beihilfe (s. d. Gl 1), nicht bloss des Geleitsmanns bei Missetat des Stammfremden gegen den Stammesgenossen.—Bessere Übs.: ‘ausl. M. i. [Plural] schadet, r. s. v. solcher Teilnahme’

The preceding sentence is generalized to the case of aiding and abetting (see that word in Gl 1), not merely that of the escort when a man of another people commits a misdeed against a fellow tribesman.—Better transl.: ‘a foreign man injures natives [plural], let him clear himself of such complicity’

in- und ut-land braucht der Agsachse zwar nicht bloss für ‘England’ und ‘Nicht-England’, sondern, im Munde fremder Sprecher, allgemeiner für ‘In-’ und ‘Ausland’ (Toller mit Compositis); hier aber, wie 6, 1¹, spricht wieder nur Englische Partei

The Anglo-Saxon does indeed use in- and ut-land not only for ‘England’ and ‘not-England’ but, on the lips of foreign speakers, more generally for ‘home country’ and ‘abroad’ (Toller, with compounds); here, however, as in 6, 1¹, it is again only the English party that is speaking
[Bessere so die zweite Anm. 2.] Hier ist Auswahleid (s. d. 6) im Ggs. zu o. 1, 2⁴ gemeint. Statt ‘[vom Gegner]’ der Übs. lies ‘[ihm]’, denn vielleicht ernannte das Gericht die Helfer

[Correct the second note 2 thus.] What is meant here is the selected oath (see that word 6), in contrast to above 1, 2⁴. Instead of ‘[by the opponent]’ in the transl. read ‘[to him]’, for perhaps the court appointed the oath-helpers
